suggestion: Retire the older deployment trees (app/ legacy, v2/, projection/, bet/, dashboard/, docs/, edge/, dash/, hub/, site/, origin/, verify/, lab/, research/, final/, and the seven audit trees) from the Pages deployment and serve only this dashboard plus a provenance archive page.
why: There are 20+ parallel page trees from earlier sessions, each with its own numbers. A reader who lands on an old tree sees a different slate and a different model and has no way to tell which is current. The dashboard links them from Earlier sessions, which is the only place they belong.

suggestion: Capture per-player game logs from the game-book PDFs already being downloaded, in the same pass that captures the team result.
why: The game books at statsdmz.nba.com already print a full per-player line for both teams. The marginal cost of parsing them alongside the final score is near zero, and it unblocks minutes redistribution, player-prop correlations and the injury-impact column in one change.

suggestion: Backfill the 2026-27 season to date (roughly 120 game days) by reading each date's official scoreboard and its game books, into a single append-only results file.
why: Every blocked strategy is blocked on sample size, not on method. The gates, the luck band, the walk-forward benchmark and the independence test (Q11) are all written and waiting for data they cannot currently get. This is the single highest-value change on this page.

suggestion: Add a closing-line feed and switch the market-anchored prior on.
why: The weight is already written as exp(-LL_model)/(exp(-LL_model)+exp(-LL_closing)) and the field is null. With a feed, every line gains a second opinion and the site can finally say whether the model or the market is better - which is the entire point of originating lines.

suggestion: Replace the per-game disagreement column with a distribution view: a small histogram of |A-B| across the window, with each game's position in it.
why: Reading 25 raw deltas requires the reader to hold the distribution in their head. The same information as a position within a distribution is read in one glance and makes an outlier game obviously an outlier.

suggestion: Show a compact sparkline of each team's measured margin over the captured log next to its rating, with a marker for the estimated rating and a band for its uncertainty.
why: A rating without a sense of its own uncertainty invites false confidence. Two games per team produce a rating with a very wide interval, and the picture would say that faster than any table.

suggestion: Add a settlement self-check that re-reads the official game book a fixed interval after settlement and raises a flag if the printed value changed.
why: Settlement currently records a stamp. If the league ever corrects a game book, this site would keep the old number with an old stamp and no warning. A delayed re-read makes a silent correction visible.

suggestion: Add a printable one-page summary that carries the slate, the two estimators' disagreement, every flagged row and the settlement state on a single sheet.
why: The dashboard is built for a screen. A one-page sheet is what someone actually carries to a review, and it would force the flagged items to the front rather than one click down.

suggestion: Publish a per-page "generated from" footer naming the exact artefact file and its hash, so a reader can verify the page matches the data without cloning the repo.
why: The pages already say which script builds them. Naming the artefact and its hash makes the claim checkable by someone reading the site rather than the repository.

suggestion: Add a third estimator that reads only schedule and rest (a pace-adjusted rest model) so disagreement becomes a three-way spread rather than a pairwise gap.
why: Two estimators can agree by luck on a given night. Three with disjoint inputs make agreement informative, and a pairwise gap gives no way to tell which of the two is the outlier when they disagree.
